headline: Subcommittee approves naming new Lowell High School academic building after Senator Edward J. Kennedy and Student Support Center after William J. Samaras
summary: The AD-HOC Building Naming Subcommittee discussed naming the new academic building at Lowell High School after the late Senator Edward J. Kennedy and the Student Support Center after William J. Samaras. Both proposals were approved by vote after comments from speakers including Ms. Dailey, Vice Mayor Nuon, and City Councilor Rourke.
decisions: Approved naming the new academic building at Lowell High School after the late Senator Edward J. Kennedy, 4 yeas.
Approved naming the Student Support Center at Lowell High School after William J. Samaras, 3 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Delrossi).

decision_evidence.quote: Ms. Martin moved to approve naming the new academic building at Lowell High School after the later Senator Edward J. Kennedy; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 4 yeas.

Ms. Martin moved to approve naming the Student Support Center at Lowell High School after the William J. Samaras; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 3 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Delrossi).

Z. Naming the Student Support Center at Lowell High School after William J. Samaras.
Chairperson Lay opened the meeting by stating that the focus of the evening's discussion would
be on naming the new academic building at Lowell High School in honor of the late Senator
Edward J. Kennedy and the Student Support Center at Lowell High School in honor of William J'
Samaras. He then opened the floor to those in attendance who wished to speak in support of
the proposed names.
Ms. Dailey addressed the subcommittee and read Senator Kennedy's biography, along with the

longstanding connection to and affection for the City of Lowell'

Vice Mayor Nuon also addressed the subcommittee and expressed his full support for naming
the new academic building at Lowell High School after the late Senator Edward J. Kennedy,
stating that he believed it would be a fitting and meaningful honor. He also spoke in support of
naming the Student Support Center after William J. Samaras, noting Mr. Samaras' significant
contributions and support to Lowell High School and support for the community.
Ms. Martin moved to approve naming the new academic building at Lowell High School after
the later Senator Edward J. Kennedy; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion
passed with 4 yeas.
Chairperson Lay then addressed the proposal to name the Student Support Center at Lowell
High School in honor of William J. Samaras, a former Head of School, City Councilor, and Mayor.
City Councilor Rourke addressed the subcommittee and expressed his strong support for naming
the Student Support Center after William J. Samaras. Drawing on his own experience as a former
Lowell High Schoolstudent, Councilor Rourke spoke about Mr. Samaras'tenure as Head of
School and the positive impact he had on students and the schoolcommunity. He highlighted
Mr. Samaras' many accomplishments and contributions to the City of Lowell and enthusiastically
urged the subcommittee to support the proposed naming.
Ms. Martin moved to approve naming the Student Support Center at Lowell High School after
the William J. Samaras; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 3
yeas, l absent (Ms. Delrossi).
Mr. Conway moved to adjourn at 5:56 p.m.; the motion was seconded by Ms. Martin. 3 yeas,
